tasks.short: Count sponges, needles and surgical instruments

steps.what: Count sponges, needles and instruments before the operation
Count the surgical items after the operation
Reconcile counts and communicate any unresolved discrepancy to the surgical team

tasks.design: Retain physical counting and discrepancy escalation under the local surgical protocol. Existing instructions in {DOCS} support the process; no automated count or new recording baseline is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: The counted objects and their location must be physically established.
tasks.enabler_now: No supported change in the digest removes that physical requirement.
tasks.still_hard: A matching total alone may not establish where every item is.
tasks.human_edge: Maintain attention and raise a discrepancy immediately despite operating-room pressure.
tasks.altitude: Counting work, accountability and decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Local count sequence and discrepancy escalation

evidence.claim: This design retains physical counts and reconciliation; the digest provides no supported surgical-item counting automation.

assumptions: Boundary is this technologist's counting and reconciliation, excluding another staff member's independent count and subsequent clinical decisions. Their time is not claimed as saved.
The technologist establishes count values directly through physical inspection. No machine consumes a structured count or free discrepancy code.
Existing native protocol access is sufficient. No new software, form or device is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Local counting protocol and division of counting responsibilities
research_questions: Where do count discrepancies arise under the current physical workflow?

incremental.description: No new workflow or system upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross saving and zero upkeep. No physical counting or safety reconciliation is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Position and drape patients for surgery

steps.what: Prepare patients by positioning them on the operating table
Cover the positioned patient with sterile surgical drapes

tasks.design: Keep patient positioning and sterile draping with the surgical team. Instructions may be read in {OTHER}, the clinical record system, but this design makes no change to physical preparation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Positioning and draping require physical assistance and sterile technique.
tasks.enabler_now: No software change is proposed for these physical actions.
tasks.still_hard: Patient condition and the planned procedure can require careful adjustments.
tasks.human_edge: Protect the patient while noticing pressure, exposure and sterility concerns.
tasks.altitude: Patient preparation responsibilities and time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Physical positioning and sterile draping retain all labour in this design.

assumptions: Boundary is the technologist's positioning and draping effort, excluding patient transport and other clinicians' simultaneous work.
Existing clinical instructions and identity checks remain under their present producers and protocol; no automated step consumes new structured input.
Test existing native instruction access if needed; no deployment is required and zero incremental upkeep follows.
unknowns: Local positioning responsibilities and patient safety procedure
research_questions: Which positions require additional trained staff or equipment?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, zero gross and net saving; physical patient preparation remains unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Continually assess operating-room conditions and needs

steps.what: Monitor operating room conditions and respond to patient and surgical team needs

tasks.design: Keep continuous situational assessment and assistance with the technologist. Existing {OTHER}, the operating-room monitoring equipment, remains available without a new model or alert layer.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task requires attention to physical conditions and spoken or unspoken team needs.
tasks.enabler_now: No new technology is needed for the retained observation and response.
tasks.still_hard: A displayed value may omit a developing problem in the sterile field.
tasks.human_edge: Anticipate needs and speak up when conditions change.
tasks.altitude: Continuous monitoring duties and time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Existing monitor runtime is not technologist labour; live assessment remains counted in full.

assumptions: Boundary is the technologist's continuous observation and response, excluding anaesthetic monitoring by other clinicians and instrument passing counted elsewhere.
No new structured needs flag or automated intervention is assumed.
Existing native monitors remain as they are; no new deployment or ongoing upkeep is added, so incremental work is zero.
unknowns: Local monitoring responsibilities and escalation arrangements
research_questions: Which changing conditions require immediate verbal escalation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross saving and zero upkeep. Existing monitoring equipment earns no new labour saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Clean and restock the operating room

steps.what: Clean the operating room according to local procedures
Gather and place equipment and supplies for the next procedure
Arrange instruments according to the procedure instructions and preference card

tasks.design: Keep cleaning, physical restocking and instrument arrangement with trained staff. A preference card in {DOCS} supports preparation; no new inventory-capture task or robotic handling is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: The room and supplies must be physically cleaned, moved and arranged.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing procedure cards already support that work.
tasks.still_hard: Availability, sterility and case-specific requirements need direct verification.
tasks.human_edge: Notice unsuitable equipment or an arrangement that would hinder the procedure.
tasks.altitude: Room preparation work and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Tray contents, sterility indicators and missing-item escalation

evidence.claim: Physical room preparation retains its labour; a digital preference card alone does not remove cleaning or handling.

assumptions: Boundary is this technologist's cleaning, gathering and arrangement effort. Sterile processing, purchase ordering and formal surgical counts are outside this task.
The procedure team supplies the existing preference card; no new structured stock or readiness flag is required by an automated step.
Test native preference-card access before adding tools. No new deployment or maintenance is introduced, justifying zero upkeep.
research_questions: Which recurring missing items delay physical room preparation?

already_counted.description: Cleaning, gathering and arranging physical supplies

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, zero gross and net saving. No physical handling or cleaning is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Surgical preparation, counts and live situational assessment retain their human time and responsibilities.
reach: Coordinate count discrepancies and room readiness with operating-room nurses
role.ambitious_version: A surgical technologist whose attention stays on the patient, sterile field and surgical team.
